Wide integer vectors

Source: R/types.R
zuint-types.Rd

Create signed and unsigned 64-bit and 128-bit integer vectors, or convert to them. Conversion is exact or gives NA with a warning of class zuint_cast_warning; it never rounds or clamps.

Usage

int64(x = integer())

uint64(x = integer())

int128(x = integer())

uint128(x = integer())

Arguments

x

A vector to convert.

Value

A vector of the requested type, the same length as x.

Details

x can be a logical, integer, double or character vector, another zuint vector, or a bit64 integer64. A double must be integral and in range. A string is decimal, 0x hex or 0b binary digits, with an optional sign, _ between digits and surrounding whitespace (see format_hex()); "NA" and blank strings are NA. NA stays NA without a warning. Names are kept.

Each type reserves one bit pattern for NA, so its range is one value short of the full width: the most negative value for the signed types and the largest for the unsigned ones.

TypeRange
int64\(\pm(2^{63} - 1)\)
uint64\([0, 2^{64} - 2]\)
int128\(\pm(2^{127} - 1)\)
uint128\([0, 2^{128} - 2]\)

int64 has class c("zu_int64", "integer64") and the storage of bit64's integer64, so code that reads integer64 reads it too.

Examples

int64("9007199254740993")
#> <int64[1]>
#> [1] 9007199254740993
uint64(c(0, 2^53))
#> <uint64[2]>
#> [1]                0 9007199254740992
int128("-170141183460469231731687303715884105727")
#> <int128[1]>
#> [1] -170141183460469231731687303715884105727
uint128(NA)
#> <uint128[1]>
#> [1] NA

# Not exact, so NA with a warning:
int64(1.5)
#> Warning: 1 value could not be represented as int64 and became NA.
#> <int64[1]>
#> [1] NA
